title: Mumbai Airport Network Outage Delays Flights, Forces Manual Check-In
excerpt: A network disruption at CSMIA on Tuesday evening hit check-in, e-gates and DigiYatra for over an hour: 18 of 44 departures between 7 pm and 9 pm left at least an hour late and three were cancelled.
body:
• A network disruption at Mumbai's Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport on Tuesday evening, October 27, forced staff to switch check-in, e-gates and DigiYatra to manual processing for over an hour.
  • Of 44 passenger flights scheduled to depart between 7 pm and 9 pm, 18 left at least an hour late and three were cancelled, according to Flightradar24 data analysed by Hindustan Times; Flightradar24 counted 327 flights held up until around 9.30 pm with average departure delays of 50 minutes.
  • Reader check: if you are flying through Mumbai, check your flight status with your airline before leaving for the airport, arrive with extra time for manual check-in queues, and do not rely on DigiYatra lanes alone during a systems outage.
  • Airport operator MIAL said manual measures kept essential operations running and reported no impact on flight operations, while airlines said delays were compounded by existing air traffic control congestion.

A network disruption at Mumbai's Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport (CSMIA) on Tuesday evening forced airport staff to switch to manual passenger processing, slowing check-ins and boarding as flight delays mounted. The outage began around 7 pm on October 27 and lasted more than an hour. Check-in counters, boarding e-gates and DigiYatra facilities were affected, Curly Tales reported, summarising coverage by The Times of India, Hindustan Times and PTI.

The CSR Journal put the start at around 7.05 pm and the duration at about 50 minutes, reporting that approximately 11 Air India flights and three IndiGo flights were affected in check-in, with gate changes, crew delays and slow boarding scanner operations also observed.

How many flights were delayed or cancelled

According to Flightradar24 data analysed by Hindustan Times, 18 of the 44 passenger flights scheduled to depart between 7 pm and 9 pm left at least an hour late, while three were cancelled. Two additional flights remained on the ground at 10.37 pm, nearly two hours after their scheduled departure. IndiGo and Air India services were among those affected.

A broader Flightradar24 count reported by Curly Tales said 327 flights were held up until around 9.30 pm, with departures recording an average delay of 50 minutes, and around 13% of flights cancelled. Both reports cautioned that it was unclear how many of those disruptions were caused directly by the network failure, because flights were already delayed by air traffic control congestion. A separate PTI report cited by other coverage also put delayed flights at 327.

That distinction matters for passengers claiming compensation or rebooking: the headline delay count for the evening is not the same as the count caused by the outage alone. The narrow, directly comparable window is 7 pm to 9 pm — 18 departures at least an hour late and three cancellations out of 44 scheduled.

What the airport and airlines said

Mumbai International Airport Ltd (MIAL), the airport operator, said teams implemented manual handling measures to reduce inconvenience and ensure essential operations continued. MIAL said the airport "experienced a temporary network disruption on Tuesday evening" and that there had been no impact on airport and flight operations so far. The operator did not disclose the precise duration of the outage or provide details on the systems affected.

The CSR Journal reported a CSMIA spokesperson confirming manual processing measures to minimise passenger inconvenience and maintain essential operations, and reiterating no significant impact on flight operations. Airlines, it reported, said their flights were already facing delays due to air traffic control congestion before the network issue, and the glitch exacerbated those challenges.

An airport official said the network was still fluctuating at around 9.36 pm as operations moved towards normal. Manual procedures kept passenger processing underway, but verification slowed and queues built during the busy evening departure period, when Mumbai handles a dense bank of domestic departures and international connections.

What travellers through Mumbai should do

For diaspora travellers connecting through Mumbai to other Indian cities, or starting a long-haul journey from Terminal 2, the practical lesson is specific. Check flight status directly with the airline before leaving for the airport rather than relying on the morning's schedule. Keep extra time for check-in when systems are in manual mode, because bag tagging and boarding-pass issue move at counter speed, not kiosk speed. Carry a printed or offline copy of your booking and ID, since DigiYatra and automatic e-gates were among the systems affected. If a connection is missed, ask the airline to record whether the cause was the network outage or air traffic congestion — the reports show both were running at once, and the recorded cause can affect rebooking handling.

Airport and airline teams were working to restore normal functioning on Tuesday night, with staff monitoring a fluctuating network. No cause for the network disruption was given in the reports.
